# Document Preparation Functions

A reusable function library for preparing a configured document, creating it or accepting an existing initialized publication, and tracking selection, admission and usability. It inherits preparation and admission behavior while adding no domain-specific terms, candidate restrictions or follow-up actions.

## Domain hooks

- `domainPrepare(prepared)` returns `{}`, stored as the entry’s `domainTerms`.
- `domainValidateCandidate(candidate, frozenTerms)` returns `true`. Here `frozenTerms` receives the stored `domainTerms`; this result adds no domain-specific rejection and does not bypass inherited checks.
- `domainNextActions(documentRef)` returns `[]`. `documentRef` contains the selected document’s `path` and `documentOrigin`; this type generates no domain-specific action descriptions.

The `checkedDomain*` wrappers reject changes to the accumulated change or event counts and enforce object, boolean and list results respectively. Next-action lists are limited to 16 Clause Response descriptions; emitted actions must name a declared `party`.

## Configuration, inputs and stored state

`preparePublic(input)` accepts `key`, `requestId`, `fields` and `values`. The resolved `key` must be nonempty text; its fallback is `single`. `prepareKeyedPublic` requires an explicit nonempty `key`. `requestId` must also be nonempty text and defaults to the resolved key. `fields` and `values` default to `{}` for intent comparison and must be accepted by the configured template.

The executing clause is identified by `clauseKey`. Its `cardinality` and `destinationBinding` are read under `/clauses/<clauseKey>/type`. With `cardinality: single`, only key `single` is accepted and the destination is the named binding’s path. Otherwise, the escaped key is appended to that path. Preparation requires a nonempty `bindings.parties` mapping.

Entries are stored under `/process_<clauseKey>/entries`, indexed by the key’s Blue ID. An entry records `key`, `requestId`, destination `path`, its own `itemPath`, and `intent`, which captures the configuration and template identities together with `fields`, `values` and `requestId`. It also records `prepared`, `requirementRef`, `domainTerms`, specialization `slots`, `obtain`, `supplier` and `status`. `requirementRef` identifies the prepared requirement; `candidateOrigin` and `documentOrigin` identify an initialized candidate’s original document, rather than its current publication.

These paths belong to the document where the functions execute, including a nested instruction’s own document. Missing state does not establish completion, readiness or a configuration default.

## Preparation and provision

Preparation rejects a changed `intent` for an existing key and rejects an occupied destination when no entry exists. Matching existing intent is recognized by `checkPreparation` as `duplicate`.

Configuration parameter `obtain` defaults to `create` and accepts only `create` or `provide`:

- `create` rejects a nonempty `suppliedParties` list. It constructs the document, configures its sources, writes it at the destination and records `documentOrigin` with status `selected`. Selection does not establish activation or usability.
- `provide` requires nonempty `suppliedBy`, stored as `supplier`. It records `awaiting_provider` and emits `Document Provision Requested`, identifying the supplier through `party` and correlating the request through `inResponseTo` and `requirementRef`. The request does not confirm that a document has been supplied.

Both modes emit `Document Prepared`, carrying `clauseId`, `itemKey`, `requestId`, `requirementRef` and the preparation status.

`providePublic(input)` takes `key` (default `single`), `document`, `inResponseTo` and `requirementRef`. The entry must exist and expect `provide`; `call/channel` must equal its `supplier`, and both correlation references must match. Provision is rejected for `reapproval_required`, `admission_denied`, `cancelled` or `cancellation_requested` entries.

The supplied `document` must contain `/contracts/initialized/document`. Its original document must match the prepared requirement after permitted specialization slots are normalized. Its effective clause policy must also match: comparison preserves clause `type`, `parameters`, `bindings`, and any `name` or `description`, with party constraints normalized. Unreviewed source changes, altered approval requirements, undeclared parties and replacement of an already staged or selected origin are rejected.

Party slots come from the template’s `/clauses/activation/parameters/parties`. Each original and current party must satisfy its configured constraint and preserve the same main party. Roles outside `suppliedParties` must also preserve the prepared main party. Any original role transport contract must agree with that party’s `lead/channel`.

`specialization/dataPaths` defaults to `[]`. Each path must identify an existing declaration, start with `/`, and neither duplicate nor overlap another slot. Reserved first segments are `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `sources`, `type`, `blueId`, `instanceKey`, `creationIntent` and `preparationContext`; an empty first segment is also rejected. Filled data must satisfy its configured constraint, and current candidate data must equal the initialized original’s data.

A valid candidate is staged with `candidateOrigin` and `candidateRef`. It can remain `admission_pending`, `awaiting_activation` or `linking`. When staging returns `ready`, provision writes the candidate publication reference at the destination, records `documentOrigin`, sets `selected` and emits `Document Selected`. A newly accepted staging operation therefore need not mean selection succeeded.

Matching preparation or provision checks can report `duplicate`, but their public wrappers still delegate to `sharedPrepare` or `sharedProvide`; those check results alone do not guarantee a retry without effects.

## Admission of additional parties

When any `bindings.sources` value is `self`, staging checks whether the executing document’s roster covers the candidate’s parties. Coverage requires matching `lead/channel` identities and nonempty matching `readerKeys`, regardless of role names. Missing parties require configured `/clauses/activation/parameters/admission/approvers` and the required Timeline Access documents. Role-name collisions receive a generated participant role.

The resulting `admissionToken` fixes the candidate, requirement, proposed parties, access documents and scope, activation revision, entry path and attempt. Its identity is `admissionRef`. A changed token requires reapproval; an existing `candidateOrigin` cannot be replaced.

Admission separates the approval grant, participant consent, access preparation and installation:

- `nextAdmissionRequest` returns an approval proposal only when appropriate; an existing pending proposal prevents another. Grant approval is checked through the admission ledger history and the matching stored token.
- Consent operations use each proposed party’s lead channel and require the current `admissionRef` plus `decision: approve` or `decline`. First consent requires `admission_pending`. Repeating the same decision is a duplicate; changing it or using a stale reference is rejected.
- An approved grant can emit `Party Addition Requested` with the proposed parties and `accessDocuments` before every participant has consented. This request neither grants private timeline access nor supplies anyone’s consent.
- Installation readiness requires every proposed party’s approval, the same activation revision and successful access validation. It sets `installing` and returns an installation request. `finishAdmission` separately requires that state and confirmed roster coverage, then records `admittedRevision`, moves to `linking` and emits progress status `admitted`.

A decline leads to `admission_denied`; a changed activation revision requires `reapproval_required`. Retirement preserves the token, consent decisions and reason, and clears a matching pending proposal.

`rebaseAdmissionPublic` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion: true`, a `call/channel` listed among admission approvers, the current `admissionRef`, and status `reapproval_required`. It clears the old token, reference and consents, increments `admissionAttempt`, retains candidate identity, returns to `awaiting_provider` and emits `reprovision_required`. It does not itself approve the new scope.

## Readiness and cancellation

Provision staging waits for `/activation/active: true` and initialized, active sources with the declared origins and roster coverage. Missing links or coverage produce `linking`; a conflicting source identity is rejected.

When `sharedRefresh` runs, it examines selected entries whose destination contains an initialized original. A changed original identity is rejected. It sets `usable` only when the selected document is active and `namedSourcesReady` succeeds; otherwise it sets `selected`. Named-source readiness also checks any applicable `selectionPath` resolves to an initialized selection of this same process. No declared source requirements means that source check succeeds. Missing initialization at the selected destination causes refresh to leave that entry unchanged.

Entering `usable` emits `Document Attached`; later loss of readiness can return the entry to `selected`. This type supplies no `nextActions`; refresh treats an absent list as `[]` for comparison. Readiness is a checked condition, not a permanent guarantee.

`cancelPublic(input)` uses `key`, defaulting to `single`. It requires an existing entry without `documentOrigin`; selected processes require domain-specific cancellation. A new request sets `cancellation_requested` and emits `Preparation Cancellation Requested`. Repeating that request returns `duplicate`. This function does not confirm cancellation or set `cancelled`.
